comment: The v0.3 local metadata class migrates to the directly used dcat:Dataset class in the incompatible v0.4 wire profile.
The identifier concept is retained while the wire predicate changes from dct:identifier to ex:datasetId.
The local name and literal semantics are retained under the v0.4 contract namespace.
The v0.3 local endpoint path migrates to the DCAT endpointURL predicate and gains a mandatory HTTPS IRI constraint.
The field migrates to dct:format and its wire value changes from JSON to application/json.
The v0.3 local update-frequency path migrates to the directly reused DCTERMS predicate.
The metadata unit field keeps its literal kWh semantics under the v0.4 contract namespace.
The v0.3 local spatial coverage path migrates to the directly reused DCTERMS predicate.
The start-date field keeps its flat xsd:date semantics under the v0.4 contract namespace.
The end-date field keeps its flat xsd:date semantics under the v0.4 contract namespace.
Direct reuse: v0.3 used dct:identifier directly; the separate migration row records its v0.4 replacement by ex:datasetId.
Direct reuse: v0.4 uses the external DCAT class IRI without a local alias.
Direct reuse: the DCTERMS title predicate remains the same IRI across the metadata migration.
Direct reuse: v0.4 uses the external DCTERMS predicate without a local alias.
Direct reuse: v0.4 uses the external DCTERMS predicate without a local alias.
Direct reuse: v0.4 uses the external DCAT predicate without a local alias.
Direct reuse: v0.4 uses the external DCTERMS predicate while constraining its value to application/json.
Direct reuse: the optional v0.4 description field uses the external DCTERMS predicate without a local alias.
Direct reuse: the optional v0.4 license field uses the external DCTERMS predicate without a local alias.
The local v0.4 identifier property expresses the DCTERMS identifier concept while preserving the D-group wire path.
The flat literal provider name approximates publisher metadata; a richer profile would use an organization node.
Schema.org provider is a close Web-metadata alignment for the flat provider-name literal.
The flat kWh literal approximates QUDT unit semantics; QUDT normally points to a unit resource.
The constrained kWh token denotes the QUDT kilowatt-hour unit concept without adopting its IRI on the wire.
The kWh token is related to a UCUM-coded representation exposed through QUDT qudt:ucumCode; lexical-system equivalence requires domain review.
The flat start date approximates the beginning of an OWL-Time interval without creating an interval node.
The flat end date approximates the end of an OWL-Time interval without creating an interval node.
The historical flat provider string approximates publisher metadata; richer graphs should use an organization node.
Schema.org provider is a common Web metadata alignment for the historical literal field.
When the provider is modeled as an organization node its display label is related to foaf:name.
The historical JSON token is related to a media type although it is not itself a media-type IRI.
The historical kWh literal denotes the QUDT kilowatt-hour unit concept without using the unit IRI on the wire.
The historical flat xsd:date field approximates an OWL-Time interval beginning.
The historical flat xsd:date field approximates an OWL-Time interval end.
The inherited record remains a lightweight SOSA observation profile in v0.4.
A building identifier can identify the feature of interest in a richer SOSA graph.
A meter identifier can identify the sensor linked through sosa:madeBySensor in a richer graph.
The literal meter identifier is only conceptually related to an SSN system implementing a sensing procedure; no equivalence is claimed.
The reading timestamp aligns with the SOSA result-time predicate.
The flat timestamp approximates an OWL-Time instant represented by an xsd:dateTimeStamp literal.
The historical mapping relates the energy reading to a SOSA result node; the hasSimpleResult row captures the literal-oriented refinement.
The numeric reading is a simple SOSA observation result while the local field also fixes the energy quantity convention.
The energy value aligns with QUDT numericValue when a richer quantity-value node is introduced.
The inherited record unit literal approximates the QUDT unit relation.
The inherited kWh token is related to a UCUM-coded representation exposed through QUDT qudt:ucumCode.
The inherited record location aligns with spatial metadata.
Schema.org location is a close alignment for the lightweight JSON node.
